purpose: Methylnaltrexone is used to relieve constipation caused by opioid pain medications like morphine or oxycodone. It is used in adults who are taking opioids for chronic pain or for pain related to advanced illness. It helps get your bowels moving again when regular laxatives have not worked well enough.
how_it_works: Opioid pain medicines can slow down your gut and cause constipation by blocking certain receptors in your intestines. Methylnaltrexone works by blocking those same receptors specifically in your gut, without affecting the pain relief you get from your opioid medication. Think of it as removing the 'brake' that opioids put on your intestines, allowing them to work more normally again.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include stomach pain or cramping, nausea, diarrhea, gas, and vomiting. Some people may also notice dizziness or feel a little lightheaded. These effects are usually mild and often happen shortly after taking the medication.
warnings: Do not use this medication if you have or suspect a bowel blockage, as it could cause a serious tear in your intestine. Rarely, it can cause a hole in the wall of the stomach or intestines, so tell your doctor right away if you have severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting. If you experience opioid withdrawal symptoms like sweating, chills, or feeling very anxious, let your healthcare provider know. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have kidney or liver problems.
typical_dosing: The injection form is usually given once every other day as needed, with at least 24 hours between doses. The tablet form is typically taken once daily by mouth in the morning, at least 30 minutes before the first meal of the day. Your doctor will determine the right dose based on your weight and kidney function. Do not take more than one dose in a 24-hour period unless your doctor instructs you otherwise.
